transcript:
This message comes from Wealthfront.
Earn a high APY on all your cash in a Wealthfront cash account.
No more juggling between checking and savings.
Just one account that delivers the best of both and makes every dollar work harder.
Get started at Wealthfront.com.
Cash account offered by Wealthfront Brokerage LLC, Member FINRA, SIPC, not a bank.
Funds are swept to program banks where they earn the variable APY.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed faced off in their first debate in
Michigan's closely watched Senate race today.
El-Sayed's trying to unite voters after a contentious primary divided Democrats.
When asked if Iran or Israel posed a more dangerous threat to the U.S., he called it
a ridiculous question and said both have been dangerous in their own way.
I don't want to be pushed into war by Israel and I don't want to be in a war with Iran.
I want our money spent here to buy schools and health care and child care here.
I don't understand why that is so inconceivable.
High profile Democrats have tried to help him bring together the coalition in recent
weeks.
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer appeared with him for the first time today since endorsing
his primary opponent.
Rogers continued to distance himself from President Trump during the debate, calling
for an end to the Iran war and an end to the tariff war with Canada.
Michigan heavily relies on trade with Canada.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nadal Hassan will be
viewed by the public.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports the U.S. hasn't had public execution since 1936.
Hegseth says members of the public will be able to watch a live stream of the execution
by firing squad, which is scheduled for December.
He said it in an interview with a right-wing news service, Real America's Voice, that was
posted on social media by an account associated with the Pentagon.
Hassan killed 13 fellow soldiers, including a pregnant woman, and wounded dozens more
on Fort Hood in 2009.
The last U.S. military execution was in 1945, of a soldier convicted of desertion.
The last public execution in the U.S. was a black man accused of raping and murdering
a white woman in Kentucky hanged in 1936.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
Curtis Flowers, whose death sentence has case reached the U.S. Supreme Court and fueled
a national debate over racial bias and jury selection, has died.
Mississippi public broadcasting's Gaylene James takes a look back at the case.
Curtis Flowers spent more than 22 years behind bars, wrongly accused of murder.
Flowers, who was black, was charged in the 1996 killings of four people at a furniture
store in Winona, Mississippi.
Over the next two decades, prosecutors tried him six times.
Then, in 2019, the Supreme Court, throughout his conviction, ruled that prosecutors improperly
excluded black jurors.
Flowers was 26 when he was arrested.
He was 50 when Mississippi dropped the charges against him in 2020.
He was 56 when he died at home on Wednesday.
No cause of death has been released.
In a statement, lawyers for Curtis Flowers write, "His name is etched into the U.S.
Supreme Court jurisprudence about what it means to fight for a fair trial free from
racial bias and the selection of jurors."
For NPR News, I'm Gaylene James in Jackson, Mississippi.
This is NPR News from Washington.
The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has returned home to San Diego after a record-setting
uninterrupted time at sea supporting the Iran war.
The deployment drew attention after reports of supply shortages, crew stress, and suicide
attempts.
The Navy initially downplayed any problems.
President Trump said the deployment was, quote, "not nearly long enough."
The former president of Bard College, Leon Botstein, has resigned from all campus-affiliated
positions amid scrutiny of his relationship with late-sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
WAMC's Mariam Ahmad reports.
Botstein resigned after the ranking Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee called for
a federal criminal investigation into his relationship with Epstein.
An email allegedly sent from the address president@vard.edu to Epstein in 2014 asked if a young woman
was, quote, "for me or are you keeping her for yourself?"
Five years later, Epstein was formally charged with sex trafficking.
Botstein denied sending the email.
He retired in June, but has remained on campus as a teacher and orchestral conductor.
Last year, student Ingrid Larsen once Botstein removed from campus.
"He needs to leave, and I think that if he doesn't, I hope that people really show up
to get him out of here."
Bard has confirmed Botstein will move out of the president's residence.
For NPR News, I'm Mariam Ahmad in Albany.
Four astronauts are back on Earth after an eight-month stay at the International Space
Station.
Their SpaceX capsule splashed into the Pacific.
They left the planet in February to replace a station crew that returned home early in
a medical evacuation.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
